name: general-seismic-benchmark-v1
purpose: Test whether the codec has a general, statistically significant advantage across independent large seismic surveys rather than favorable small patches.

selection_policy.large_survey_sampling: For seismic payloads >25 GB, sort eligible seismic objects deterministically by canonical object/path name, form cumulative payload bytes, and select three disjoint complete-file spans centered near 10%, 50%, and 90% of cumulative bytes. Grow each span using complete files until it reaches at least 10 GB. Never choose spans using compression results, signal statistics, or visual inspection.
selection_policy.small_survey_sampling: For seismic payloads <=25 GB and >=5 GB, use the complete seismic payload.
selection_policy.unit_weighting: Each independent survey counts once in headline win-rate/median-gain statistics regardless of byte size. Also report a separate byte-weighted aggregate.
selection_policy.error_contract: For each survey benchmark unit, epsilon = 0.10 * global standard deviation of all selected numeric seismic samples. Require max absolute reconstruction error <= epsilon for every sample.
selection_policy.payload_contract: Benchmark numeric seismic amplitudes. File/container headers and acquisition metadata are excluded identically from all lossy codec byte counts; any codec-specific model/framing/selector bytes are counted.
selection_policy.no_retuning: Codec design and global hyperparameter menu must be frozen before headline test results are examined. Dataset-specific model fitting is allowed only when the decoder can reproduce it from transmitted or already-decoded information and all required bytes are charged.
